goal: The terminal tab is a real terminal on macOS and Windows: a pty behind a full emulator, so interactive programs, prompts, colours and resizing work as they do in PowerShell or Ghostty, with the ownership contract (one shell per tab, a journal, a verified stop) unchanged.
scope: A. node-pty inside the owned worker: a login shell on macOS, PowerShell 7 (or Windows PowerShell) through ConPTY on Windows; the service gains raw write and resize and keeps line input for the ownership contract
B. xterm.js in the tab: keystrokes to the pty, bytes to the emulator, fit on resize, the app's theme, ⌘F find, copy on select, links, the assistant's command mirror, Clear and Restart
C. Ghostty as an engine: ghostty-web (Ghostty's VT core in WebAssembly, xterm-compatible surface) chosen in Settings › General, loaded only when chosen, falling back to xterm.js when it cannot load
D. Windows: the ownership tour and the interactive tour in the real app on a hosted Windows runner (.github/workflows/terminal-windows.yml, on demand)
acceptance: Interactive programs run in the tab on macOS: a prompt that reads input, less on the alternate screen, colours, a resize the shell sees; the login shell with TERM=xterm-256color (tour)
On Windows PowerShell runs through ConPTY inside the owned Job with the same ownership journal and verified stop (hosted Windows runner)
The assistant's commands still mirror into the tab; ownership refusals and the unverified-shutdown path are unchanged (unit tests)
A Ghostty-based engine can be chosen in Settings and passes the same tour, or the reason it cannot is recorded

truthReview: 2026-10-04: the terminal tab is a pty (node-pty 1.1.0 in the owned worker: login shell on macOS, PowerShell 7 or Windows PowerShell through ConPTY on Windows) behind xterm.js 6, with ghostty-web 0.4.0 as a chosen engine. Proven on this Mac (four tours: two engines, two themes, eleven checks each; ownership unit tests 10/10; ownership tour; journey 76/76; the packaged app in the earlier nightly) and on a hosted Windows runner at be728eaf (https://github.com/FRIKKern/barkdown/actions/runs/37162736078): node-pty spawns PowerShell through ConPTY under Electron's node, unit tests 10/10, the ownership tour in the real app (commands, profile switch, killed app, explicit start, quit, legacy launch; five owned workers verified stopped) and the interactive tour with thirteen checks on each engine (Read-Host answered live, a one-key read, colours, resize, Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V, the alternate screen, find, the mirror strip, themes, restart). Found and fixed on the way: white text in the light theme (a light-dark() colour xterm.js cannot parse); the assistant's mirrored lines overwritten by ConPTY, now a strip of their own under the terminal on both platforms; the text read breaking at soft wraps; Playwright's page never answering on a Windows runner when video recording is on (tests only). Corrections to earlier statements: hosted Windows runners were available (the Actions budget block was September's; the zero-job failures were visual.yml's duplicate key, now removed). Limits: on Windows the Ghostty engine does not paste with Ctrl+V; a Ghostty tab keeps its open-time theme and has no Find; the Windows proof is a hosted runner from source, not the packaged app and not the owner's machine; no Windows nightly exists. Delivered for macOS in v0.6.0-nightly.20261003.3 (chain receipt on b684800f).
